_comment: initial-version sets the first release to 0.1.0. With no release tag yet,
release-please ignores the 0.0.0 in the manifest and falls back to its own
default of 1.0.0 (it proposed exactly that in #4). initial-version only
applies while no release exists, so it needs no cleanup after 0.1.0. A
release-as would have to be removed again after 0.1.0, and a Release-As
commit footer is worse: it stays in the history and tix had it proposed
again, as a downgrade, five times. No last-release-sha either: nothing to
include-component-in-tag is false because the dart strategy takes the
pubspec name as the component, which would tag tix_mobile-v0.1.0. The
release workflow and the README expect plain v0.1.0.
draft is true because release.yaml builds the binaries and publishes the
release as its last step, so a release is never visible without its
downloads. See the comments in release-please.yml.
